statement: Loading a GenBank file converts every feature location from the file's 1-based inclusive coordinates to 0-based half-open in-memory intervals: for NC_001699.1 (JC polyomavirus, 5130 bp, circular) the subject's 28 Annotations must carry exactly the intervals and strands listed below, in file order, where a file location a..b becomes the interval (a-1, b).

parameters.conversion: file a..b (1-based, both ends inclusive) -> in-memory (a-1, b) (0-based, end exclusive)

statement: Exporting converts back the other way, losslessly: for every feature of NC_001699.1 and AF071878.1, re-reading the subject's own GenBank export with Bio.SeqIO must give the same integer intervals, the same part order and the same strand as reading the original file — i.e. the round trip through the subject's 0-based half-open model is the identity on coordinates, and every feature's extracted subsequence is byte-identical to the one extracted from the original record.

parameters.compared: [(int(p.start), int(p.end)) for p in feature.location.parts], feature.location.strand, str(feature.extract(record.seq))
parameters.oracle: Bio.SeqIO.read on the pinned bytes vs Bio.SeqIO.read on the subject's export

statement: A join() keeps every part, in order, across load and export — including an origin-spanning join on a circular record, which INSDC documents as the way a feature that crosses the origin is written (`CDS join(2004..2195,3..20)`). NC_001699.1's `rep_origin join(5118..5130,1..12)` and AF071878.1's `stem_loop join(1975..1993,1..19)` must survive with both parts, in that order, and the exported record must still say `circular`.

parameters.outer_bounds_note: min/max across parts is the whole molecule (0, record_length) for an origin-spanning feature; that is the documented meaning of Annotation.start/end, so the parts list is what must carry the truth.

statement: complement() and complement(join()) keep their strand and their part order. NC_001699.1's `CDS complement(join(2603..4426,4771..5013))` loads as a minus-strand feature whose parts are in 5'-to-3' feature order — Biopython's writer states the convention explicitly ('we expect the CompoundLocation and its parts to all be marked as strand == -1, and to be in the order 19:100 then 0:10'), i.e. descending on the minus strand — and must export as `complement(join(2603..4426,4771..5013))` again, with the exon whose bases are 4771..5013 read first.

statement: Partial boundaries survive the round trip. INSDC gives `<` and `>` a meaning no exact coordinate carries — `<1..888` means the feature starts before the first sequenced base — so a record whose file says `<108..1007` must not be exported as `108..1007`. The three partial boundaries in the pinned real records must still be partial in the subject's export.

parameters.detected_by: type(location.start) is Bio.SeqFeature.BeforePosition / type(location.end) is AfterPosition, or the literal '<'/'>' in the exported FEATURES block
parameters.why_int_comparison_misses_it: BeforePosition(5) == ExactPosition(5) is True, so any check that compares int(start) cannot see the loss.

statement: order() must not be exported as join(). INSDC defines them as different assertions — join means the elements 'should be joined (placed end-to-end) to form one contiguous sequence', order means only that they 'can be found in the specified order ... but nothing is implied about the reasonableness about joining them' — so rewriting one as the other changes what the record claims.

parameters.probe_bases: the first 300 bases of gx/corpus/inputs/AF071878.1.gb, so the record under test carries real sequence
parameters.companion_control_note: a real join() in the same record must still export as join(): fixing order() must not be done by breaking join()

statement: A remote reference part — INSDC's `J00194.1:100..202`, 'bases 100 to 202, inclusive, in the entry ... with primary accession number J00194' — must be preserved or the feature rejected. It must never be exported as a bare local interval, because that silently reassigns the feature to this record's own bases 100..202.

statement: An edit that does not touch a feature's bases leaves that feature's extracted subsequence byte-identical. For NC_001699.1, after each of the pinned edits below, every feature the edit does not overlap must extract exactly the string it extracted from the unedited record.

parameters.untouched_definition: a feature is untouched by [start, end) when no part (p_start, p_end) satisfies p_start < end and p_end > start; for an insert (start == end) a feature is untouched when no part satisfies p_start < start < p_end
parameters.oracle: str(feature.extract(record.seq)) computed from the pinned bytes with Bio.SeqIO before the edit

statement: A feature downstream of an insert or delete shifts by exactly the net length change, and a feature upstream does not move — checked by re-deriving each interval by index from the raw sequence, not by the subject's own arithmetic. For each pinned edit, a part (p_start, p_end) entirely at or after the edit end becomes (p_start + delta, p_end + delta) and a part entirely at or before the edit start is unchanged, where delta = inserted - (end - start).

parameters.edits: the four edits pinned in CO-8
parameters.oracle: the shifted interval re-derived by index: new_seq[p_start + delta : p_end + delta] must equal old_seq[p_start : p_end]

statement: A feature whose bases are entirely deleted must be reported as lost, not kept. Deleting exactly [5073, 5090) from NC_001699.1 — the whole of `repeat_region 5074..5090` — leaves no bases for that feature to describe, so it must appear in the dropped list. It must not survive as a zero-length annotation, which the exporter renders as the INSDC between-position `5073^5074`, a location that per the Feature Table 'points to a site between bases' and asserts something the original record never said.

parameters.every_exported_location_must_name_a_real: a GenBank location counts from 1, so no exported location may contain the token 0; deleting the record's first 12 bases must not produce `0^1`.

statement: A feature that spans an edit is either adjusted so everything it asserts is still true, or reported as lost — never kept with a stale assertion. Deleting one base inside NC_001699.1's `CDS 526..1560` changes that CDS's own bases, so either the feature is dropped, or its `/translation` qualifier is updated; keeping `526..1559` (1034 bases, not a multiple of three) with the original 344-residue `/translation` exports a record whose stated protein does not translate from its stated bases.

acceptable_outcomes: the CDS is in the dropped list
the CDS is kept and its /translation equals str(extract.translate(table=1, to_stop=True)) of the edited bases

statement: Reverse-complementing a record maps every feature onto the new strand without changing what the feature reads: for every feature, `extract` on the reverse-complemented record must return exactly the string `extract` returned on the original record, because reverse-complementing a molecule does not change which bases a gene is made of or the order it reads them in. This must hold for compound features too — a spliced CDS's exons must still be listed in 5'-to-3' feature order, which for a minus-strand CompoundLocation means descending coordinates.

parameters.interval_map: [s, e) on the forward strand becomes [L - e, L - s) on the reverse complement, L = 5130
parameters.note: applying the map twice is the identity for any part order, so a flip-flip round trip cannot see an order error; the extract is what pins it.

statement: The GenBank and the EMBL serialisation of one INSDC record describe the same molecule to the subject. For AF071878.1 — NCBI's GenBank flat file and EBI's own EMBL flat file, each fetched from its archive — `read_genbank` and `read_embl` must return the same sequence, the same length, the same topology, and for every feature key present in both files the same parts, strand and extracted subsequence.

parameters.archive_difference: NCBI's copy additionally carries three `gene` features (indices 2, 4, 6) that ENA's copy does not; that is a real difference between the two archives, not a subject defect, so agreement is asserted over the five feature keys both files contain.

statement: The sequence-edit endpoint must not silently discard the record's annotations and topology. POST /sequences/{id}/edit stores the edited molecule under a new id; that stored record must carry the record's features — shifted for the edit, the way the GUI's own edit path does via shift_annotations — and must keep `is_circular`, because the stored record is what the file endpoints then export.
